appraisal_events.evidence: elle était pour moi une amie admirable et sincère
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator gives a direct, unqualified compliment to Andrée, setting her sincerity apart from her unreliable husband.

appraisal_events.evidence: Odette, qui en avait un aussi beau, de l'exhibition duquel elle-même avait abusé, regardait, maintenant qu'elle était en « tenue de guerre » à l'imitation des dames du faubourg, avec sévérité
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette now imitates the sober wartime restraint of the faubourg ladies and judges newcomers' ostentatious pearls with severity, an elevation into arbiter status that the narrator undercuts by recalling her own earlier abuse of the same display.

status_effects.explanation: Direct narrator praise establishes Andrée as a genuinely admired and sincere friend.

Odette's adoption of faubourg wartime restraint and her severe judgment of others' ostentation aligns her with elite taste, though the narrator's ironic aside about her own past excess tempers the elevation.

ambiguities: Odette's positioning as an arbiter of sober wartime taste is undercut by the narrator's reminder that she herself once flaunted a similarly showy pearl necklace, so the direction of her local status shift is genuinely mixed rather than a clean elevation.

The remark that 'on trouvait qu'elle ne pourrait rien ajouter au brillant milieu' about Odette was treated as part of the already-accepted Mme Verdurin movement (explaining surprise at the advances) rather than scored as a distinct event for Odette.
